Implement and enforce security controls, patch management, and compliance policies.
Respond to and resolve system or network security incidents
Administer and support Microsoft Office 365 and cloud-based services.
Manage Citrix environments and Microsoft Cloud applications.
Support ERP systems, databases, and university-specific applications.
Liaise with vendors for upgrades, licensing, and technical support.
Assist the IT Operations & Infrastructure Manager with capacity planning and infrastructure improvements.
Contribute to IT projects, process improvements, and digital transformation initiatives.
Support IT governance, compliance, and alignment with the University’s goals.
About you:
Qualifications and Skills required:
Qualification in ICT, with a high level of knowledge gained through ongoing professional
development and training with at least 2 years of corporate experience in ICT or 3 years equivalent work experience, with at least 1 year in a systems administrator capacity.
Experience managing ERP systems and databases (e.g., SQL Server, Oracle).
Knowledge of ITIL framework and service management practices.

25786.description:
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
The Geotechnical Engineer will support safe and efficient mining operations by providing operational geotechnical monitoring, analysis, inspections, and technical input to identify and manage geotechnical and geothermal hazards.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Assist with ground control management, slope monitoring, data analysis, and field inspections to minimize risk to safety and production in a dynamic geothermal environment.Conduct routine geotechnical inspections of pit walls, dumps, stockpiles, harbour waste platform, and marine dumps.
Monitor slope stability using radar, prism, GNSS, and other monitoring systems.
Review and analyse monitoring data and report abnormal movement or trends.
Assist with geotechnical drilling, logging, mapping, and instrumentation programs.
Support slope reconciliation through Design, Implementation, and Verification processes.
Assist with geotechnical and geothermal risk assessments and implementation of controls.
Prepare technical reports, monitoring summaries, and presentations for stakeholders.
Support investigations into ground movement, instability, and incidents.
Provide input into short- and medium-term mine planning and operational designs.
Assist in maintaining and improving geotechnical monitoring systems and databases.
Support technical mentoring programs under guidance of senior engineers.
Actively promotes and demonstrates safe work practices and compliance with site HSE requirements.
Works collaboratively with geotechnical, mining, planning, survey, and operations teams.
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Minimum of 2–4 years’ experience in open pit geotechnical engineering or related mining roles.
Experience in slope monitoring, field inspections, and geotechnical data collection.
Exposure to operational mining environments is desirable.
Sound understanding of open pit geotechnical principles and ground control practices.
Awareness of operational safety and risk management systems.
Working knowledge of PNG Mine Safety Act and Regulations.
Competency in MS Office applications.
Knowledge of slope stability monitoring and analysis software.
Basic knowledge of geological and mining modelling software (e.g., Minesight).
Familiarity with cost control systems (e.g., SAP).
Good verbal and written communication skills.
Strong analytical and problem solving abilities.
Good organisational and time management skills.
Ability to work independently and within a team environment.
Working Conditions
You’ll be part of the Geotechnical team on a 22:20 roster, requiring hands-on engagement and collaboration across disciplines.
If you feel that you could make a meaningful contribution in this role, we encourage you to discuss this opportunity with your current people leader and how it aligns with your longer term career goals.
To support you in your application, we have created a range of resources available to all Newmont People including information on eligibility criteria and FAQs. Find out more by visiting our page in Discovery: Internal Employee Resources
As a current employee or contractor, please submit your application is MS Word or Adobe format online via the Internal Job Postings link on Discovery.
If you have issues applying through Discovery or would like to learn more about the role before applying, please contact the relevant member of our Talent Acquisition Team.
Apply

25716.description:
Credit Corporation is recruiting a suitable candidate for the role of
Senior Internal Audit – CCSI & CCPL.
The
Senior Internal Auditor will provide critical support to the Head of Group Internal Audit by conducting comprehensive audits to assess the effectiveness of our risk management practices. This role will contribute to the overall success of the organization by ensuring integrity, and reliability of our financial information.
Key Responsibilities:
Internal Audit Planning & Risk Assessment
Contribute to the development and execution of a risk-based Internal Audit plan aligned with the organization’s risk profile, including oversight of operational and financial audits.
Provide proactive risk and control assurance through participation in key business and technology initiatives, as well as conducting ad hoc reviews and investigations.
Audit Execution, Compliance & Internal Controls
Conduct thorough audits of financial statements, operational processes, and internal controls to identify risks, errors, and irregularities.
Assess compliance with policies, procedures, regulations, and industry best practices, and report any deviations to management.
Stay updated with changes in laws, regulations, and accounting standards, recommending adjustments to internal controls and processes as needed.
Process Improvement & Value Creation
Identify and communicate control deficiencies and recommend practical solutions to address identified risks and improve process efficiency.
Review and evaluate operational processes to identify opportunities for cost savings, revenue enhancement, and process improvement.
Collaborate with management to develop action plans to address audit findings and monitor the implementation of corrective actions.
Reporting, Issue Tracking & Stakeholder Communication
Prepare and review high-quality audit reports, presenting findings, conclusions, and actionable recommendations to senior management and stakeholders.
Track, follow up, and ensure timely closure of all open audit issues.
Coordinate with external auditors to optimize audit efforts and leverage Internal Audit work effectively.
Leadership, Quality Assurance & Audit Function Management
Lead and supervise a team of auditors, providing guidance, coaching, and performance evaluations.
Ensure Internal Audit complies with professional standards and incorporates best practices.
Maintain audit technology platform leveraging support from the information systems as needed.
Qualifications and Skills
Education:
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business or a related field is mandatory
Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) or Certified Public Accountant (CPA) is mandatory
Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE). Not essential but preferred.
Experience:
More than three (3) years of work experience as an Auditor (Internal/External)
Proven knowledge of auditing standards and procedures, laws, rules and regulations
Experience in Oracle ERP, Finpower Connect, Core Banking System is highly desirable
Experience in performing financial, operational, and compliance audits
Experience in the banking and finance industry would be well regarded.
Technical Skills:
Proficient in using audit software and other data analytical tools
Technology Proficient (excel, word, PowerPoint, Visio, ability to learn new software)
Advanced report writing and audit documentation skills.
Application process:
If you think you have what it takes to be in this role, we would like to hear from you.

A cover letter.

Position Description
Role Purpose
A member of the Senior Management Team (SMT), the People and Culture Manager (PCM) will report to the Country Director and have a matrix (functional) reporting line to the IP People & Culture Business Partner in Melbourne. The role is responsible for leading development of organisational culture and staff engagement, providing effective human resources management, administration and technology support to the Country Program. The role is responsible for all People and Culture (P&C) service delivery in country, including but not limited to setting and ensuring compliance with P&C policy and processes, recruitment, performance management processes, industrial and employee relations and operational HR services.
Key Areas of Accountability
Business Partnering
Provide quality advice on all Human Resources (HR)-related issues to the SMT and individuals, to ensure program expectations and goals are achieved.
In partnership with the Country Director, inspire and lead the development of a strong organisational culture and drive staff engagement strategies.
Manage and lead staff development and performance process, including the annual staff appraisal process through communication with managers, support for the process, training for managers, training for staff etc.
Research resources for professional development that aligns with Save the Childrn in PNG (SCiPNG) Country Strategic Plan and maintain dialogue with managers relating to recommendations made on performance appraisals.
Develop and implement an annual PNG People Plan.
Facilitate key cyclical people processes including annual performance cycle, remuneration, and talent reviews.
Work with the PNG Country Director to develop a performance culture, including ensuring robust performance processes (goal setting, reviews, improvement plans) are in place and follows
Oversee in-country recruitment and general HR Plans with each project to aid in prioritising project recruitments to avoid unnecessary delays to implementation.
Employee Relations
Review all SCiPNG policies and practices to ensure compliance with PNG employment and industrial relations laws (including compliance with PNG Common Rule Awards).
Build leadership capability to manage performance and employment related issues in a professional manner.
Develop and maintain employment-related policies and procedures and ensure their consistent application across the organisation.
Develop and maintain relationships with the Department of Labour and Department of Immigration to inform all aspects of engagement of non-citizens and compliance with the Employment Act, including the provision of accurate advice on new hires to hiring managers.
Consult with employees and managers on employee grievances and lead and advise on disciplinary matters.
Implement disciplinary procedures in accordance with SCPNG HR policies and provide advice and training to managers on performance management (poor performance) issues.
Operational HR Management
Ensure an appropriate efficient and consistent level of customer services is delivered across to all staff.
Assist project, area, and function managers in matters relating to employee relations, occupational health and safety, and staff training.
Oversee facilitation of Immigration requirements for international staff.
Ensure SCiPNG is compliant with all statutory obligations.
Ensure maintenance and management of staff benefits; superannuation, medical/life insurance and worker’s compensation cover.
Manage the transition of the payroll function to Finance; interim management of payroll processing, reconcile reporting with Finance.
Maintain confidential and up-to-date personnel files including accurate records of staff annual leave, TOIL, and sick leave.
Ensure timely submission of monthly headcount reports to SCA HR.
Provide regular recruitment progress updates to SMT and Hiring Managers.
Ensure all new staff receive a full induction and complete mandatory training within three (3) months.
Ensure the exit procedures for departing staff including the final letter, severance, exit interviews, and final payment advice to payroll where applicable.
Implement and embed people related reporting (attendance, leave, mandatory learning) and ensure People Managers demonstrate accountability for operational management.
Ensure thorough processing of staff on-boarding, induction and off-boarding.
Leadership
Lead by example and actively foster a team culture of inclusion, agility, client centricity, continuous improvement, and performance.
Ensuring the right mix of skills to deliver on the PNG P&C team’s agenda, actively invest in peer, colleague, and team development.
Act as a change agent for new ways of working (empowered, agile, cross-functional teams).
Develop and nurture strong partnerships with key leaders, setting the tone for engagement at all levels.
Attend P&C Community of Practice monthly meetings, scheduled workshops, and training.
Attend National Development of Counsel- HR Community of Practice routine meetings.
Serves as a role model and mentor for staff, demonstrating Save the Children’s values.
Strengthen the capacity of HR/Admin staff and focal points in field offices to ensure competencies to appropriate effective and efficient service.
Country Administration Management: IT, Local Facilities
Oversight and line management of IT function including ensuring staff have appropriate tools and services to fulfil their role.
Management of local IT contracts in partnership with and reference to the Head of Infrastructure in Group Technology.
Report on key IT and asset performance metrics and issues arising to SMT.
Oversight and line management of Office Administration functions.
Ensure all office locations are in a safe, clean and promote staff wellbeing and that any visitors are appropriately received.
Oversight of leased properties ensuring contracts are fit for purpose and up to date, including overseeing renegotiation as required and holding landlords to account for compliance with their legal and contractual obligations. Partner with the Property Manager in Group Operations & Risk
Managing subletting as required and reporting on issues arising to SMT.
Health and Safety
Act in a safe manner at all times, including complying with all safety instructions and training given at the workplace.
Participate in, and contribute to, health and safety awareness and improvements.
Be aware of, and consider, the risks associated with your team’s everyday work and ensure appropriate mitigation measures are applied.
Ensure staff have completed all required training and have up-to-date background and working with children checks.
Lead and promote a culture of strong governance promoting employee health, safety and security and operational risk management.
Show leadership towards health and safety awareness and improvements.
General
Comply with Save the Children policies and practice with respect to child safeguarding, code of conduct, health and safety, equal opportunities and other relevant policies and procedures.
Embody the Save the Children values in practice of Accountability, Ambition, Collaboration, Creativity, and Integrity. Work according to Save the Children’s mandate and child focus.
Work according to any other duties as assigned by the supervisor.
Person Specification
Essential knowledge or experience
Knowledge and understanding of the PNG employment Act and industrial relations laws.
Demonstrated experience in working alongside national staff in a culturally sensitive manner to build capacity.
Significant experience leading professional development of staff.
Ability to effectively establish a learning culture within an organisation.
Experience in successfully establishing and managing collaborative relationships with department heads.
Strong representation and influencing skills.
Experience managing a diverse workforce, including effective performance management and utilisation of capacity building, coaching, and mentoring skills.
Demonstrated use of positive coping strategies in fast-paced environments.
Fluency in written and spoken English.
Experience in the NGO/International Development Sector
Papua New Guinean working privileges (PNG citizen preferred)
Required qualifications and/or accreditations
Bachelor’s Degree in human resources management or relevant field.
Minimum of eight (8) years of work experience in HR and/or related field.
More than three (3) years in an HR or Operations Manager role.
Multiple Roles:
"We are actively seeking talented individuals to join our organization on various positions at different location within our organisation. If you are passionate about Children’s rights and have the drive to contribute to a dynamic environment, we encourage you to apply."
Save the Children is no ordinary not-for-profit.
We’re ambitious, creative and outspoken. We stand up for children’s rights. We want all children to be educated, healthy and live a life free from violence. We’ve been supporting communities in Papua New Guinea for 40 years and are committed to be a platform for transformative and lasting change for children their families, and their communities.
Here you’ll make a difference
Save the Children is the world’s largest independent child rights development organisation, making a difference to children’s lives in more than 100 countries. From emergency relief to long-term development, Save the Children secures a child’s right to health, education, and protection. At Save the Children, we attract bright and big-hearted people who are inspired to make a difference. Together, we are fearless in our pursuit of making lasting change for the children and communities who need it most. In Papua New Guinea, Save the Children currently implement programs in the sectors of health, education, child protection, child rights governance and livelihoods.

24929.description:
Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


Joining our commercial team, the Team Lead – Contracts provides leadership and guidance to the Contracts team, ensuring high standards of contract administration, negotiation, and compliance. This role combines mentoring of team members with a strong technical focus, taking a lead role in procurement planning and market engagements under the direction of the Principal and Superintendent – Contracts. The position plays a pivotal role in achieving effective commercial outcomes, strengthening supplier relationships, and ensuring compliance with company policies, procedures, and applicable legislation.


Key Accountabilities


Key accountabilities of this position include.




Provide day-to-day leadership, mentoring, and guidance to Contracts Officers, fostering capability development and professional growth.


Allocate tasks, set priorities, and oversee workload to ensure deadlines and quality standards are consistently met.


Conduct regular feedback, coaching, and performance development for team members.


Act as a role model in professional conduct, supplier engagement, and commercial practice.


Oversee the drafting, review, and negotiation of contractual agreements to secure favourable terms and conditions.


Personally handle high-value or complex contracts to ensure strategic alignment and optimal outcomes.


Ensure all contracts comply with legal requirements, organisational policies, and industry standards.


Identify and mitigate potential contractual risks to protect the organization's interests.


Monitor compliance with contractual obligations, escalating significant risks, disputes, or performance issues to the Superintendent/Principal as appropriate.


Conduct audits and reviews of contract performance, ensuring adherence to obligations.


Foster and maintain strong relationships with vendors and service providers.


Act as a primary point of contact for contractual matters, facilitating communication and collaboration with external partners.


Collaborate with internal departments, including operations, supply and finance, to support contract-related initiatives.


Drive improvements in procurement and contract management processes, including development of templates, evaluation methods, and best practice approaches.


Capture and share lessons learned from market engagements to strengthen future strategies.


Stay abreast of industry trends, regulatory changes, and emerging risks incorporating these into contract strategies.


Provide training and guidance to internal teams on contract management processes and best practices.




About You 


To be considered for this role, it is essential that you




Degree Qualified tertiary qualifications in a relevant field (business or legal etc) essential.


Procurement or contract management certification (e.g., CIPS, WCC, or equivalent) desirable.


5 – 8 years’ relevant work experience in a Commercial Contracts role, preferably in mining or similar environment.


Demonstrated knowledge of contract administration, negotiation, and management.


Strong experience in leading tenders, supplier evaluations, and market engagements.


Demonstrated behaviours consistent with K92 Mining core values.


Demonstrated problem solving and decision-making capability.


Strong commercial analysis and evaluation capabilities.


Demonstrated ability to mentor, coach, and develop team members with diverse skills and backgrounds.


Demonstrated ability to communicate clearly to, and influence, internal and external stakeholders.


Experience communicating with vendors in PNG and internationally.


Proficient in the operation of Pronto (desirable)


Experience in Microsoft suite office tools




Life at K92  


K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.


In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster. 


THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

25711.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a
Technician Mechanical Fitter – Oxygen Plant
, you will play a key role in maintaining three oxygen plants to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operation. You’ll apply your mechanical fitting skills to fabricate components, interpret technical drawings, troubleshoot issues, and support continuous improvement across the oxygen plant area. Safety is central to this role—you’ll follow all HSE requirements, understand hazards before starting work, and stop any unsafe activity. Working within a diverse team, you’ll contribute to production performance, uphold maintenance standards, and actively identify opportunities to reduce costs and improve work quality.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Ensure full compliance with company HSE policies, including Fitness for Work.
Strong understanding of hazard identification tools
Have experience working in Oxygen plants
Have experience with following work orders and basic work management skills
Work constructively within a diverse team and contribute positively to team outcomes.
Safely operate and maintain hand and power tools.
Demonstrate strong team behaviours—asking questions, raising issues, contributing ideas, seeking clarity, requesting feedback, and stopping unsafe work.
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
You’ll thrive in this role if you bring strong mechanical fitting capability, a commitment to safe work practices, and a collaborative, proactive approach to maintenance.
Mechanical trade qualification certified to NATTB
Ability to follow procedural steps and complete practical, hands‑on tasks.
Practical judgment to solve problems or seek assistance when needed.
Willingness to learn and improve work methods through experience and observation.
Competence in mechanical fitting, fabrication, and interpreting technical drawings.
Ability to build positive working relationships across different disciplines.
Determination, persistence, and commitment to delivering productive, high‑quality work.
Alignment with Newmont’s values, culture, and expectations for safe and reliable operations.
Your Work Environment
This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, PNG.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
Newmont offers a dynamic and inclusive workplace where your expertise drives real impact. You’ll have opportunities for professional growth, contribute to innovative projects, and be part of a team that values safety, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Apply

25710.description:
Don’t come for an easy career. Stay for a rewarding one.
Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.
We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.
At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.
Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas supplier, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project.
For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.
What you’ll do:
Based in Papua New Guinea at Ridge Camp, the Operations Training Team Lead works closely with the PNG Business Unit Field Operations and Maintenance teams to ensure competency-based training and assessment are delivered in line with business priorities.
The role is the primary interface between the Manager Operations Readiness and PNG Field Trainers, with direct oversight of all training execution, logistics, and coordination across PNG operations. You will be responsible for the intake, coordination, and ongoing support of first-year apprentices in PNG.
Key Responsibilities:
Liaise with the Operations Leadership Team, Manager Operations Readiness, and the Competency-Based Training and Assessment (CBTA) team to prioritise frontline training needs for field personnel.
Lead PNG-based trainers in the implementation of CBTA across the PNG business.
Coordinate the delivery of training through in country and external training providers.
Coordinate mobilisation and group travel for PNG BU personnel undertaking out-of-country training.
Execute the intake of first-year apprentices and maintain accountability for apprentices during their institutional training year.
Work collaboratively with the CBTA team and key stakeholders to evaluate training and assessment outcomes and drive continuous improvement.
Liaise with the PNG National Apprentice and Trades Training Board (NATTB) regarding the Santos PNG Apprentice Program.
Manage and deliver training-related projects as assigned.
Administer the Learning Management System (SuccessFactors) in support of competency-based training and assessment.
Contribute to the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of Santos’ competency-based training and assessment framework.
Ensure compliance with the Santos Management System (SMS), Delegation of Authority (DOA), and corporate governance and safety requirements.
What you’ll bring:
To be successful in this role, you will bring extensive operational experience combined with a proven background in training and competency assurance.
Essential
Minimum 10 years’ experience in oil and gas process or production operations.
At least 5 year’s experience in a training or learning delivery role.
Demonstrated experience in training and competency assurance systems, including competency-based training and assessment.
Proven experience in administration and working with Learning Management Systems, such as SuccessFactors.
Cert IV TAE40116, Cert IV TAE40122 or higher
Australian PMA 02/08 Cert III/IV or trade qualifications
Desired
Relevant Tertiary qualifications or trade background
SuccessFactors LMS or equivalent.
What you’ll get:
Here, you’ll be amongst high-calibre people and get to work on industry-leading projects. We don’t shy away from solving tough problems at pace. We like it that way. You can expect to be challenged and supported; to learn and grow.
At Santos, we’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive. This means a place that is safe; where you are valued and respected, and your contribution is recognised and appreciated. Join us, and you’ll play a role in this too.

25702.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As Advisor, Maintenance Autoclaves, you’ll coordinate maintenance activities for 4 autoclaves and associated equipment, driving KPI compliance and continuous improvement. Your leadership will help ensure safe, efficient, and reliable operations, contributing directly to shutdown readiness, statutory compliance, and process plant improvements.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Administer and optimize maintenance activities and weekly schedules
Ensure strict compliance with safety protocols
Lead and guide supervisors, trades, and new employees
Conduct inspections, safety audits, and troubleshoot issues
Compile performance reports and maintain accurate records
Assess risks and implement mitigation measures
Collaborate with internal teams and external contractors/suppliers
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Fitter and turner trade certificate is preferred
5 years experience in maintenance coordination and safety compliance
Experience with autoclaves is essential
Experience with positive displacement pumps (GEHO’s)
Advanced skills in maintenance scheduling, safety audits, and troubleshooting
Strong knowledge of maintenance management systems (SAP) and risk management
Effective communication, self-awareness, and teamwork abilities
Commitment to Newmont’s values and productive work culture
Your Work Environment
This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, PNG, working within the Autoclave Maintenance department.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
Newmont offers a dynamic and inclusive workplace where your expertise drives real impact. You’ll have opportunities for professional growth, contribute to innovative projects, and be part of a team that values safety, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Apply

Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.

Auto Electrician
to join our team on a permanent full-time position at our Simberi Operation. Your work location is Papua New Guinea, working a 15/13 Roster from Kavieng, Rabaul, Port Moresby, Lae, Mt Hagen, Madang, Goroka, Alotau, Wapenamanda, Popondetta, Hoskins, Vanimo, Wewak or Tabar group of Islands.

We need the best people. People who have drive, energy and are genuinely passionate about the work they do and provide a positive impact. Additionally, we need people who see a challenge as an opportunity for growth and value working with others towards a common goal.​

Essential

Forklift Licence and Drivers Licence
Understand relevant engineering standards and associated procedures
Strong communication skills and the ability to effectively manage time

Developing initiative and problem-solving skills
Field experience

Simberi Operations

Ancillary HE Fitters
Simberi Gold Company Limited forms part of the St Barbara Group. Our Simberi Operations consists of an open cut mine on the northernmost island in the Tabar group of islands in the province of New Ireland in Papua New Guinea. Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.​​
We are currently seeking
Ancillary HE Fitters
to join our team at the Mobile Maintenance Workshop on a permanent, full-time position at our Simberi Operation. Your work location is Papua New Guinea, working a 15/13 roster from Kavieng, Rabaul, Port Moresby, Lae, Mt Hagen, Buka, Madang, Goroka, Alotau, Wapenamanda, Popondetta, Hoskins, Wewak, Vanimo or Tabar group of Islands.
(Locals are encouraged to apply)
.
Reporting to the Mobile Maintenance Supervisor, the Ancillary HE Fitter is responsible to provide Mechanical Maintenance of Ancillary Equipment (as designated), while ensuring health, safety, environmental, and quality workmanship standards are maintained.
The opportunity
Technical accountabilities
Ensuring safe work practices, own health and safety and all other workers by identifying hazards and ensuring issues and risks are reported and addressed.
Complete tasks to ensure the department reaches safety and equipment performance targets.
Ensuring all statutory requirements of the role are met around ancillary equipment including classified plant.
Ensuring all tasks are carried out in an environmentally sustainable manner.
Contributing productively as a member of the Simberi Maintenance Team.
Work to reduce unplanned breakdowns and re-work.
Thorough record keeping.
Compilation and adherence to JHAs, SWPs and SOPs.
Scheduling Accountabilities
Participate in training provided by the business.
Actively participate and promote a safe working environment, participate in Departmental safety meetings and display a safety conscience attitude in accordance with the OH&S policies and procedures, and safe working practices.
People Accountabilities
Promote and adhere to the company’s internal methodologies, policies, procedures and standards by consistently maintaining a high quality of work across all allocated functions.
We need the best people. People who have drive, energy and are genuinely passionate about the work they do and provide a positive impact. Additionally, we need people who see a challenge as an opportunity for growth and value working with others towards a common goal.​
We would love to hear from you if you have​:
Essential
Behaviour consistent with St Barbara’s Values
Current unrestricted PNG Driver Licence
NATTB Trade qualification in Heavy Equipment Fitting or Automotive Electrician
Minimum 4 years industry experience
Strong ability to work effectively within a team
Strong communication skills
Ability to work to tight deadlines on multiple tasks
High level of enthusiasm for the work with high performance goals
Good attention to detail
Desirable
Certificate to perform dogging CPCCLDG3001A or RIIHAN208D.
Certificate to operate non- slew crane TLILIC3006A or RIIHAN212D.
Prepared to work out of hours as required.

25496.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
This position reports to the Supervisor, Asset Protection and will be responsible for ensuring the safety of our growing gold site at Eastern Highlands.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Ensure asset protection and compliance with company policies, security standards, and safety regulations, including voluntary principles on security and human rights.
Monitor, inspect, and maintain security systems and conduct searches to prevent unauthorized items, theft and tampering.
Safeguard valuables and personnel through vehicle escort duties, perimeter patrols, and rapid response to emergencies or law-and-order issues.
Manage crisis situations and emergency preparedness, including fire and rescue training, arresting illegal miners, and making swift decisions during incidents.
Perform administrative and liaison duties, such as clearance of terminated employees, reporting suspicious activities, and collaborating with Community Relations on security matter
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have
Have at least 3 years or more in a mining environment but must have worked previously as police, correctional services, or military personnel or similar with no criminal record.
Possess training equivalent to Police/Correctional or Military.
PNG Drivers Licence
Strong leadership and decision-making skills.
Excellent interpersonal and negotiating skills.
Can be able to manage the safety and/or security and asset protection department.
Physically fit and healthy.
Prepare clear, concise, and accurate investigative and narrative reports
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply
